key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict and optimize the tensile strength and micro-hardness of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints from key welding parameters.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a fast surrogate model for selecting welding conditions, helping improve weld quality and reduce trial-and-error in intelligent manufacturing.
method: Inputs: TRS, TTS, and TPD; outputs: UTS and micro-hardness
Compared LR, RF, SVR, XGBoost, and KNN on experimental FSW data
Used an 80:20 train-test split with MAE, RMSE, RAE, and RRSE
evidence_signal: Random Forest gave the best UTS prediction on testing data (MAE 9.007 MPa, RMSE 12.975 MPa), while SVR with RBF kernel performed best for micro-hardness (MAE 0.923 HV, RMSE 1.155 HV).
watch_item: The model performance is based on a relatively limited experimental dataset, so broader validation is needed before deployment across other alloys or tool geometries.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning approach for predicting mechanical characteristics of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints
